messages:
Maria Valdez: Quick question 025-07 review cycle overlapped with my parental leave. Im out 2025-06-15 to 2025-08-15. How do reviews / calibration / comp decisions work if I'm on leave?

Erik Johnson: Congrats Maria! Ill defer to People Ops but my preference is we don't rush anything while you're out.

Jordan (People Ops): Congrats Maria. Two common options: 1) Defer the review until you return and apply the same cycle (no penalty), or 2) run a limited-scope review while you're on leave if you prefer to keep timeline for promotions/comp. Both are allowed; we try to avoid disadvantaging leave-takers.

Maria Valdez: If we defer, does that delay any salary increase or promotion until after Im back?

Tasha (Compensation): If deferred, comp changes are applied effective the normal cycle date once the review completes. We can also do an interim retroactive increase to the original effective date in rare cases. If timing matters for budget reasons, we can discuss making the increase effective on return.

Erik Johnson: Would it help to do a lightweight self-update and manager note so we have context when you come back? No pressure to answer while away.

Maria Valdez: Id prefer to defer but want to make sure calibration won't treat me as \"no data.\"

Jordan (People Ops): Good call. Please do the following before leave: 1) Upload a 1-paragraph \"leave context\" note to your review (why deferred, dates), 2) Erik add a short manager note. That tells calibration committees the deferral is intentional.

PeopleOpsBot: Reminder: Policy link for reviews & leave: https://hr.redwood.com/policies/reviews-and-leave (internal).

Tasha (Compensation): Also note: eligibility windows for promotion buckets are preserved if the deferral is documented. We will not re-run performance windows unfairly. If you opt in to a limited review while away, we will accept asynchronous input (manager + self) and allow you to record a short voice note when back if you want to add context.

Maria Valdez: Thanks. Any impact on stock vesting or bonuses?

Jordan (People Ops): Vesting continues per standard schedule while on paid leave. For discretionary bonuses tied to mid-year goals, teams can pro-rate or keep full award depending on agreed expectations. Documenting the plan with your manager before leave avoids surprises.

Erik Johnson: I'll add the manager note and mark the review \"deferred due to parental leave\". Maria, please upload your one-paragraph note today if possible.

Maria Valdez: Uploading now. Appreciate the clarity 6#128522;

PeopleOpsBot: Ticket created: HR-REVIEW-3344 - \"Maria Valdez - review deferral for parental leave\". Jordan assigned.

Jordan (People Ops): Follow-ups: Jordan to confirm comp implications with Tasha; Erik to add manager note; Maria to upload context. We'll loop back before calibration.

Maria Valdez: Thanks everyone!\"
